en: meeting to launch the New Year

examples.ko: 연초 시무식에는 임직원이 모두 대강당에 모여요.
examples.en: At the New Year launch ceremony, all the staff gather in the main hall.
This year's opening ceremony is held on the morning of January 2.
At the opening ceremony, the CEO announced this year's goals.
Our company keeps the New Year opening ceremony simple.
After the opening ceremony, I ate rice cake soup with my teammates.

examples.ko: 시무식 때 입을 정장을 미리 챙겨 놓았어요.
examples.en: I got my suit ready in advance for the opening ceremony.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 새해 첫 출근일에 하는 행사예요. 반대로 한 해를 마무리하는 행사는 '종무식'이라고 해요. '시무식을 하다', '시무식을 열다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is the event a company or organization holds on the first working day of the new year. The event that wraps up the year is called '종무식'. You say '시무식을 하다' or '시무식을 열다'.

examples.en: The number of people taking part in civic movements is growing.

examples.ko: 이 동네에서는 시민운동으로 공원을 지켜 냈어요.
examples.en: In this neighborhood, a civic movement saved the park.
A civic movement to reduce waste spread across the country.
My mother has been involved in civic movements for a long time.

examples.ko: 시민운동 단체가 거리에서 서명을 받고 있어요.
examples.en: A civic group is collecting signatures on the street.
In college, I was active in a civic movement club.

explain: 정부나 회사가 아니라 일반 시민이 스스로 모여 사회 문제를 바꾸려는 활동에 써요. '시민운동을 벌이다', '시민운동을 펼치다'처럼 '벌이다/펼치다'와 자주 함께 나와요. '시민운동 단체'처럼 뒤에 다른 명사를 붙여서도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used for activities in which ordinary citizens, not the government or companies, get together to change a social problem. It often goes with '벌이다' or '펼치다', as in '시민운동을 벌이다'. It is also commonly followed by another noun, as in '시민운동 단체'.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 다음 달부터 시범적 운영에 들어가요.
examples.en: This app goes into pilot operation next month.

examples.ko: 먼저 한 학교에서 시범적 수업을 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: We will try a pilot class at one school first.

examples.ko: 시범적 도입이라서 아직 불편한 점이 많아요.
examples.en: Since it is only a trial introduction, there are still many inconveniences.

examples.ko: 시청은 시범적 사업으로 무료 자전거를 빌려줘요.
examples.en: The city hall lends free bicycles as a pilot project.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 새 메뉴를 시범적으로 판매하고 있어요.
examples.en: That shop is selling the new menu item on a trial basis.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 재택근무를 시범적으로 해 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our team decided to try working from home as a trial.

explain: '시범적 운영', '시범적 도입'처럼 본격적으로 하기 전에 먼저 해 보는 일 앞에 와요. '시범적으로'의 꼴로도 많이 써요. 반대로 정식으로 크게 시작할 때는 '본격적'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes before things you try out before doing them fully, as in '시범적 운영' or '시범적 도입'. It is also very often used in the form '시범적으로'. The opposite, for a full-scale start, is '본격적'.

examples.ko: 말끝마다 시비조로 말하는 사람과는 대화하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: It is hard to talk with someone who picks a fight in every sentence.

examples.ko: 그의 시비조 말투에 기분이 확 나빠졌어요.
examples.en: His confrontational way of speaking really put me in a bad mood.
Why do you keep picking a fight with me?

examples.ko: 손님이 시비조로 따지는 바람에 직원이 당황했어요.
examples.en: The customer argued in a belligerent tone, and the staff member was flustered.
Even to the hostile question, the teacher answered calmly.

examples.ko: 요즘 형은 시비조여서 말 붙이기 어려워요.
examples.en: My brother has been so combative lately that it is hard to talk to him.

explain: '시비를 걸다'처럼 싸움을 걸듯이 따지고 드는 말투나 태도를 말해요. 보통 '시비조로 말하다', '시비조의 말투'처럼 써요. 말하는 방식을 나쁘게 평가할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes a tone or attitude that sounds like picking a fight, like '시비를 걸다'. It is usually used as '시비조로 말하다' or '시비조의 말투'. It is a negative judgment about the way someone speaks.

examples.ko: 사소한 일이 시빗거리가 되어 크게 싸웠어요.
examples.en: A trivial matter became a point of dispute and we had a big fight.
That remark soon became a subject of controversy.
I was careful with my words so as not to create anything to argue about.

examples.ko: 이웃끼리 주차 문제로 시빗거리가 끊이지 않아요.
examples.en: The neighbors never run out of things to quarrel about over parking.
The meeting ended quietly with nothing to argue over.
That one photo was the source of the dispute.

explain: 말다툼이나 논란이 될 만한 일을 말해요. '시빗거리가 되다', '시빗거리를 만들다', '시빗거리로 삼다'처럼 써요. '논란'보다 사람들 사이의 다툼 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It refers to something that could cause an argument or controversy. You say '시빗거리가 되다', '시빗거리를 만들다' or '시빗거리로 삼다'. Compared with '논란', it feels more like a quarrel between people.

examples.en: I felt envious of my friend's success.

examples.ko: 언니는 동생에 대한 시샘 때문에 토라졌어요.
examples.en: My older sister sulked out of jealousy toward her younger sibling.

examples.ko: 그녀는 시샘 어린 눈으로 나를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: She looked at me with envious eyes.

examples.ko: 시샘을 부리지 말고 같이 기뻐해 줘요.
examples.en: Don't be jealous, and be happy for them together.

examples.ko: 남의 시샘을 살 만큼 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: He is popular enough to make others jealous.
That comment came out of jealousy.

explain: '질투'나 '시기'와 비슷하지만 친구나 형제 사이에서 샘내는 가벼운 느낌으로 많이 써요. '시샘이 나다', '시샘을 부리다', '시샘을 사다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '질투' or '시기', but it often has a lighter feel of envy among friends or siblings. Common patterns are '시샘이 나다', '시샘을 부리다' and '시샘을 사다'.

examples.en: My friends are jealous of my new bag.
The younger sister was jealous of her older sister's popularity.
Don't be jealous, and congratulate them together.
If you envy others, only your own heart gets tired.
A cold wind blows as if envying the spring.

examples.ko: 다들 시샘할 만큼 두 사람은 사이가 좋아요.
examples.en: The two get along so well that everyone is jealous.

explain: '친구를 시샘하다', '친구의 성공을 시샘하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. '질투하다'보다 가볍게 샘내는 느낌이고, 연인 사이의 질투에는 '질투하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '봄을 시샘하는 추위'처럼 날씨에 비유해서도 써요.
explain_en: It takes an object with '을/를', as in '친구를 시샘하다' or '친구의 성공을 시샘하다'. It feels lighter than '질투하다', and for jealousy between lovers '질투하다' sounds more natural. It is also used figuratively for weather, as in '봄을 시샘하는 추위'.

examples.en: There is a test drive of the new car this afternoon.

examples.ko: 시승을 해 보고 나서 차를 사기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to buy the car after taking a test drive.

examples.ko: 시승은 예약한 사람만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who made a reservation can take a test drive.
The reporters who took part in the test drive left their reviews.
The test drive reviews were good, so I went with high expectations.

examples.ko: 이번 시승 차량은 새로 나온 전기차예요.
examples.en: This test-drive car is the newly released electric car.

explain: 사려고 하거나 새로 나온 차를 직접 타 보는 것을 말해요. '시승을 하다', '시승 행사', '시승 후기'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '시운전'은 만들거나 고친 차를 시험 삼아 운전해 보는 것이라 차이가 있어요.
explain_en: It means actually riding or driving a car you are thinking of buying or a newly released car. It appears in '시승을 하다', '시승 행사' and '시승 후기'. The similar '시운전' is about trial-running a car that was just built or repaired, so it differs.

examples.en: I test-drove a new car over the weekend.
You can test-drive an electric car at the showroom.

examples.ko: 직접 시승하면 승차감을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you test-drive it yourself, you can feel how it rides.

examples.ko: 시승하지 않고 차를 사는 건 불안해요.
examples.en: Buying a car without test-driving it makes me uneasy.
I keep thinking about the car I test-drove yesterday.
Reporters test-drove the new model first.

explain: '차를 시승하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요. 자주 '시승해 보다'의 꼴로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '타 보다'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It takes an object with '을/를', as in '차를 시승하다'. It often appears as '시승해 보다'. In everyday talk people also just say '타 보다'.

examples.en: My senior always makes only silly jokes.
The movie was so lame that I left halfway through.
Instead of fooling around, why don't you study?

examples.ko: 제 눈에는 그의 말이 다 시시껄렁해요.
examples.en: To me, everything he says is worthless chatter.

examples.ko: 시시껄렁하다고 무시하지 말고 끝까지 들어 봐요.
examples.en: Don't dismiss it as trivial; hear it through to the end.
I miss the silly stories from back then.

explain: 쓸데없고 가치 없다고 깔보는 느낌이 있는 말이에요. '시시하다'보다 거칠고 구어체에 가까워서 사람의 말이나 행동에 자주 써요. 상대방에게 직접 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It carries a sense of looking down on something as pointless or worthless. It is rougher and more colloquial than '시시하다', and is often used about a person's words or actions. Saying it directly to someone can sound rude.

examples.en: I got scolded for giggling and chatting with a friend in class.
The kids in the back are giggling and chatting.
Stop messing around and get some work done.
What are you two giggling about like that?

examples.ko: 시시덕거리는 소리 때문에 집중할 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't concentrate because of the sound of idle chatter and laughter.
At the team dinner, I joked around with my coworkers.

explain: 별 의미 없는 말로 웃고 떠들 때 쓰고, 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '수다 떨다'가 이야기를 나누는 것이라면 이 말은 쓸데없이 웃고 장난치는 모습에 가까워요. '시시덕대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is used for laughing and chatting about nothing in particular, with a slightly negative feel. While '수다 떨다' is about talking, this word is closer to laughing and goofing around pointlessly. '시시덕대다' has the same meaning.

examples.ko: 그들이 싸운 이야기를 듣고 시시비비를 가려 주었어요.
examples.en: After hearing why they fought, I sorted out who was right and wrong.

examples.ko: 이 사건의 시시비비는 법원이 판단할 거예요.
examples.en: The court will decide who is right and wrong in this case.

examples.ko: 시시비비에 휘말리고 싶지 않아서 자리를 피했어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to get caught up in the dispute, so I left.

examples.ko: 그는 사소한 일에도 시시비비를 따지기 좋아해요.
examples.en: He likes to argue over who is right even about small things.
He clearly knows right from wrong, so I trust him.

examples.ko: 시시비비와 상관없이 일단 사과하는 게 어때요?
examples.en: Regardless of who is right, why not apologize first?

explain: 옳고 그름을 뜻하고, 거의 '시시비비를 가리다', '시시비비를 따지다'의 꼴로 써요. '시비'만 쓰면 '시비를 걸다', '시비가 붙다'처럼 싸움이 되는 말다툼의 뜻이 되니 구별하세요.
explain_en: It means right and wrong, and is used almost always as '시시비비를 가리다' or '시시비비를 따지다'. The shorter '시비' on its own, as in '시비를 걸다' or '시비가 붙다', means a quarrel, so keep them apart.

examples.ko: 설날에 시아주버니 댁에 먼저 인사를 드리러 갔어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, we first went to greet my husband's older brother's family.
My husband's older brother gave the kids some pocket money.
I get along well with my husband's older brother.
I called my husband's older brother to ask how he was doing.
My husband's older brother and his wife are coming this weekend.
It was my husband's older brother's birthday, so the whole family gathered.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 남편의 형을 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아주버님'이라고 해요. 남편의 남동생은 '시동생'이라고 해서 따로 불러요.
explain_en: A married woman uses this to refer to her husband's older brother. When addressing him directly, people usually say '아주버님'. Her husband's younger brother is called '시동생', a separate word.

examples.en: The new product demonstration is held tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 이번 시연회는 본 행사 전의 예행연습이라고 생각하세요.
examples.en: Please think of this demo as a rehearsal before the main event.
I was invited to a demo and saw a robot for the first time.
The team members prepared all night before the demonstration.
The screen suddenly went off during the demonstration.

examples.ko: 시연회에서 앱 사용법을 직접 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: At the demo, they showed us how to use the app in person.

explain: 제품이나 기술이 실제로 어떻게 작동하는지 직접 보여 주는 자리예요. 영화를 미리 보여 주는 행사는 '시사회'라고 해서 달라요. '시연회를 열다', '시연회에 참석하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is an event that shows in person how a product or technology actually works. An event that previews a film is called '시사회', which is different. You say '시연회를 열다' or '시연회에 참석하다'.

examples.ko: 백화점에서 새로 나온 차 시음 행사를 해요.
examples.en: The department store is holding a tasting event for a newly released tea.

examples.ko: 시음은 무료라서 부담 없이 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: The sampling was free, so I tried it without any pressure.

examples.ko: 시음을 해 보고 마음에 드는 걸 샀어요.
examples.en: I tried a sample and bought the one I liked.

examples.ko: 시음용 커피가 작은 컵에 담겨 있었어요.
examples.en: The sample coffee was served in small cups.

examples.ko: 시음 코너 앞에 사람들이 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: People lined up in front of the tasting corner.
The customers who joined the tasting rated the flavor.

explain: 사기 전에 맛보라고 조금 마셔 보게 하는 것을 말해요. 먹는 음식은 '시식', 마시는 음료는 '시음'이라고 구별해요. '시음 행사', '시음용', '시음회'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It means letting people sip a little of a drink to try before buying. For food you eat, the word is '시식', and for drinks it is '시음'. You see it in '시음 행사', '시음용' and '시음회'.

examples.ko: 오후 세 시쯤 되니 시장기가 돌아요.
examples.en: Around three in the afternoon, I start to feel a little hungry.
I ate a piece of bread to take the edge off my hunger.

examples.ko: 시장기 때문에 수업에 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: I can't focus in class because I'm hungry.

examples.ko: 시장기도 없는데 친구가 먹자고 해서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wasn't even hungry, but my friend wanted to eat, so I ate.

examples.ko: 시장기는 약간 느껴지는데 아직 밥때는 아니에요.
examples.en: I feel a bit hungry, but it's not mealtime yet.
Gimbap eaten when you're hungry tastes really good.

explain: '배고프다'보다 약하게, 슬슬 출출한 느낌을 말해요. '시장기가 돌다', '시장기를 달래다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '출출하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a milder, peckish kind of hunger than '배고프다'. It is used in '시장기가 돌다' and '시장기를 달래다'. A similar word is '출출하다'.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 시장성이 높아서 투자자가 많아요.
examples.en: This product has high marketability, so it has many investors.
The marketability is good, but the price is a problem.

examples.ko: 아이디어는 좋지만 시장성을 따져 봐야 해요.
examples.en: The idea is good, but we need to check whether it will sell.
It was a product that wouldn't sell, so they stopped production.

examples.ko: 그 책의 시장성에 대한 평가가 엇갈려요.
examples.en: Opinions are split on how well that book will sell.
Our team leader always checks marketability first.

explain: 상품이나 아이디어가 시장에서 팔릴 가능성을 말해요. '시장성이 있다/없다/높다'처럼 써요. 상품 자체의 품질과 완성도를 말하는 '상품성'과는 초점이 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to how likely a product or idea is to sell in the market. You say '시장성이 있다', '시장성이 없다' or '시장성이 높다'. It differs a little from '상품성', which focuses on the quality and polish of the product itself.

examples.en: The granddaughter waits on her grandmother at her side.
In the old days, servants waited on their masters.

examples.ko: 아픈 남편을 시중드느라 쉴 틈이 없었어요.
examples.en: I had no time to rest because I was taking care of my sick husband.

examples.ko: 시중들 사람이 없어서 제가 직접 했어요.
examples.en: There was no one to attend to things, so I did it myself.

examples.ko: 그는 하루 종일 손님을 시중드는 일을 해요.
examples.en: His job is attending to guests all day.
My stamina dropped a lot while I was looking after the patient.

explain: 옆에서 식사나 몸 씻기 같은 자잘한 일을 돌봐 주는 것을 말해요. ㄹ이 있는 동사라서 '시중드는', '시중드세요'처럼 ㄹ이 빠지는 활용에 주의하세요. '시중을 들다'로 띄어 써도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means staying beside someone and taking care of small needs such as meals and personal care. The final ㄹ drops in some forms, as in '시중드는' and '시중드세요', so watch the conjugation. You also often see it written as '시중을 들다'.

examples.en: As the current saying goes, kids these days live a 'god-tier life'.

examples.ko: 시쳇말이 너무 많아서 이해가 안 돼요.
examples.en: There is so much trendy slang that I don't understand it.
Trendy slang goes out of fashion quickly.

examples.ko: 교수님이 수업에서 시쳇말을 써서 웃음이 터졌어요.
examples.en: The professor used trendy slang in class and everyone burst out laughing.
It would be fun to make a dictionary of trendy slang.

examples.ko: 시쳇말에 약한 아버지는 늘 뜻을 물어보세요.
examples.en: My father is weak on trendy slang and always asks what it means.

explain: '시쳇말로'의 꼴로 가장 많이 써요. 이야기 중간에 요즘 표현을 끌어와 '요즘 말로 하면'처럼 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '요즘 말로'가 더 흔하고, 시쳇말은 글이나 방송에서 자주 보여요. 비슷한 말로 '유행어'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is most often used as '시쳇말로', to bring in a current expression in the middle of a story, like 'in today's words'. In daily talk '요즘 말로' is more common, and 시쳇말 shows up more in writing and broadcasts. A similar word is '유행어'.

examples.en: After going up and down the stairs, my knees ache.
My elbow joint was sore, so I went to the hospital.
My wrist aches, but it's bearable.
I put a pain patch on my aching shoulder.

examples.ko: 찬 바람을 맞으면 이가 시큰거리기 시작해요.
examples.en: When I'm hit by cold wind, my teeth start to feel sensitive.
Watching the sad movie, my nose stung with emotion.

explain: 관절이나 이가 시리고 저린 듯한 약한 통증이 계속될 때 써요. 슬프거나 감동받았을 때 코끝이 찡한 느낌에도 비유해서 써요. 같은 느낌을 '시큰하다'로도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes a mild, lingering sore or stinging feeling in joints or teeth. It is also used figuratively for the stinging feeling in your nose when you are sad or moved. The same feeling can be expressed with '시큰하다'.

examples.en: My knees ache, so stairs scare me.

examples.ko: 달리기를 한 뒤로 발목이 계속 시큰시큰해요.
examples.en: My ankle has kept aching since I went running.
I massaged my aching shoulder and it got a bit better.
If your teeth keep feeling sensitive, go see a dentist.
My wrist aches, but I have to work.
My nose stung at the moving scene.

explain: '시큰하다'를 되풀이해서 시큰한 느낌이 계속 이어지는 모습을 나타내요. 관절이나 이의 통증 외에 코끝이 찡할 때도 써요. 하나의 순간적인 느낌보다는 이어지는 느낌에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It repeats '시큰하다' to show the sore or stinging feeling continuing. Besides pain in joints or teeth, it can describe a stinging nose when moved. It suits a lingering feeling better than a single momentary one.

examples.en: After walking a long time, my right ankle is sore.
My knee was sore, so I slept badly.
My nose stung and tears came.

examples.ko: 어깨가 시큰한 걸 보니 비가 오려나 봐요.
examples.en: My shoulder aches, so it must be going to rain.
Reading the letter, my heart ached.

examples.ko: 날이 추우면 손목이 시큰할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: When it's cold, my wrist sometimes aches.

explain: 관절이나 이가 시리고 약하게 아픈 느낌을 나타내요. 감동이나 슬픔 때문에 코끝이나 가슴이 찡할 때도 써요. '시큰둥하다'는 모양이 비슷하지만 뜻이 완전히 달라서 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It describes a mild, cold-and-sore feeling in joints or teeth. It also describes a stinging nose or aching heart when you are moved or sad. '시큰둥하다' looks similar but means something completely different, so don't mix them up.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 언제 터질지 모르는 시한폭탄이에요.
examples.en: This problem is a time bomb that could blow up at any moment.
People are saying that household debt is a ticking time bomb.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 시한폭탄 같은 위험을 안고 있어요.
examples.en: That plan carries a risk like a time bomb.
I feel like I'm living with a time bomb.
An abandoned old building is like a time bomb.
An aging population is called a time bomb for our society.

explain: 실제 물건보다 '곧 큰 문제로 터질 위험'을 비유할 때 뉴스와 대화에서 많이 써요. '시한폭탄 같다', '시한폭탄이나 다름없다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 막대한 빚이라는 시한폭탄을 안고 있어요.
phrases.en: This company is sitting on a time bomb of huge debt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당장은 괜찮아 보여도 곧 크게 터질 수 있는 위험을 품고 있다는 비유예요. 주로 뉴스나 토론에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for carrying a risk that may blow up soon even if things look fine now. It is mostly used in news and debates.
phrases.en_equiv: sit on a ticking time bomb

explain_en: It is used far more often as a metaphor for a danger that will soon explode into a big problem than for the actual device. It appears in news and conversation, as in '시한폭탄 같다' or '시한폭탄이나 다름없다'.

examples.en: After lunch, drowsiness hits me.

examples.ko: 식곤증 때문에 오후 회의 내내 졸았어요.
examples.en: I dozed through the whole afternoon meeting because of post-meal sleepiness.
I drank coffee to shake off my after-lunch sleepiness.
For post-meal sleepiness, a light walk is good.

examples.ko: 식곤증과 싸우는 오후 두 시가 제일 힘들어요.
examples.en: Two in the afternoon, when I fight post-meal drowsiness, is the hardest.
Anyone can get sleepy after a meal.

explain: 밥을 먹은 뒤에 나른하고 졸린 것을 말해요. '식곤증이 오다', '식곤증이 몰려오다'처럼 써요. 봄에 나른하고 졸린 '춘곤증'과 짝으로 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It means feeling sluggish and sleepy after eating. You say '식곤증이 오다' or '식곤증이 몰려오다'. It is worth learning alongside '춘곤증', the springtime sluggishness.

examples.en: The biggest pleasure of traveling is enjoying food.
I went on a food trip to Busan.

examples.ko: 식도락을 즐기는 편이라 맛집을 많이 알아요.
examples.en: I enjoy eating out, so I know a lot of good restaurants.
Since I got into food exploring, I've gained weight.

examples.ko: 제 취미는 식도락이라서 주말마다 새 식당에 가요.
examples.en: My hobby is food exploring, so I go to a new restaurant every weekend.
This city is famous for its food scene.

explain: 맛있는 음식을 찾아 먹으며 즐기는 일이나 취미를 말해요. '식도락 여행', '식도락을 즐기다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '맛집 투어'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the hobby or pleasure of seeking out and enjoying good food. It is often used as '식도락 여행' or '식도락을 즐기다'. In daily talk people also say '맛집 투어'.

examples.ko: 사고 후 식물인간이 되었던 환자가 깨어났어요.
examples.en: A patient who had been in a vegetative state after an accident woke up.

examples.ko: 그 환자는 식물인간 상태로 오 년을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The patient spent five years in a vegetative state.

examples.ko: 식물인간을 돌보는 가족의 어려움을 다룬 기사예요.
examples.en: It's an article about the hardships of families who care for patients in a vegetative state.
This movie is about a patient in a vegetative state and a nurse.
Could a family's voice help even a person in a vegetative state?
The family of a person in a vegetative state needs help from those around them.

explain: 뇌가 크게 다쳐서 의식이 없지만 숨은 쉬는 환자를 가리키는 말로 뉴스나 영화에서 나와요. 의학에서는 '식물 상태'라고도 해요. 사람을 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서, 환자를 직접 이렇게 부르지는 않아요.
explain_en: It appears in news and films for a patient with serious brain damage who has no consciousness but still breathes. In medicine it is also called '식물 상태'. It can sound demeaning, so people don't call a patient this directly.
